findings.question: Q1 (read + measured). Effective order of PlayerChoiceInput, PlayerMatchInput, PlayerDriveInput, Unit, Weapon, Shot, MatchController, RoundRestartInput inside one physics frame.
findings.answer: Per frame: PlayerDriveInput x2, PlayerMatchInput x2, PlayerChoiceInput x2 (all priority -1, tree order); then priority 0 in tree order: Map nodes (Ford, FuelCan), Unit 1, Unit 2, PlayerFireInput x2, any Shots, MatchController, RoundRestartInput (process_mode ALWAYS); last the two Weapons (priority +1). So Self-destruct, Unit and Shot all run before MatchController. The Weapon does NOT come before Shot/MatchController: it is the last node of the frame.
findings.evidence: READ priorities (only _ready() assigns): weapon.gd:42,76 (unit 0 +1 = +1); player_fire_input.gd:32,63 (weapon -1 = 0); player_match_input.gd:45,91, player_drive_input.gd:26,65 (unit -1 = -1); player_choice_input.gd:45,84 (controller -1 = -1). Unit, Shot, MatchController, RoundRestartInput assign none (default 0); RoundRestartInput is process_mode ALWAYS (split_screen.tscn:218). Tree order in split_screen.tscn: World:43 {Map:46, Player1Unit:49, Player2Unit:53, DriveInputs:57/62, MatchInputs:67/73, Weapons:79/86, FireInputs:93/98, ChoiceInputs:103/110}, Views:123, Divider:202, MatchController:212, RoundRestartInput:217. A Shot is add_child'ed to unit.get_parent() = World (weapon.gd:113): after World's last child, before MatchController. MEASURED (probe pf_order and pf_order_map, notes in every _physics_process, 60 frames each, greybox field and Map 01, no pause): one relative order in every frame, only the number of Shots (0/1/2) and a destroyed Unit not ticking vary: 'Drive1,2 > Match1,2 > Choice1,2 > [Ford W/E, FuelCans] > Player1Unit > Player2Unit > Fire1,2 > Shot.. > MatchController > RoundRestartInput > Weapon1,2' (live tree indices on Map 01: Units 440/447, MatchController 528, RoundRestartInput 529). A Shot fired in frame N first ticks in N+1 (f=14->15, f=26->27, both runs), never in N. Logs: pf-engine/out/pf_order.log, pf_order_map.log.
findings.recommendation: Write this order into MatchController's class doc as the contract the loss check relies on (destruction sources: Self-destruct -1, Unit/Shot 0 earlier in the tree; Weapon +1 and RoundRestartInput after the controller destroy nothing). Add a regression assertion in the loss scenario (see Q2/Q3) because the guarantee rests on default priority 0 plus tree position, not on a declared priority.

findings.question: Q2 (measured). Frame of Unit.destroyed vs frame of the MatchController's next _physics_process, per destruction source. Is the controller's tick of the same frame after the destruction?
findings.answer: Yes for every source the game has: Tab, Enter, a Shot kill, a Gyrocopter Fuel crash and apply_damage from a coroutine after physics_frame all destroy inside the physics step before the controller's tick (frame delta 0). Only sources outside that part of the step miss it: apply_damage from the idle phase (after process_frame) is taken by the very next step's controller tick, and a node ordered after the controller (priority +5) is taken one frame later. No game node is such a source.
findings.evidence: MEASURED, probe pf_q2 (ran on greybox, Map 01 headless fixed-fps, and windowed real-time; identical relations in all three). Final headless run (pf-engine/out/pf_q2.log), destroyed.emit frame -> controller tick frame: a1 Tab f=15->15; a2 Enter f=203->203; a1b Tab injected in the idle phase (real-keyboard timing) f=394->394; a3 Tab+Enter on one step f=582 (both)->582; b Shot kill (P1 held fire 93 ticks, 8 shots of 5 dmg on 40 hp; lethal Shot tick note n=15880, destroyed n=15882, controller tick n=15885) f=879->879; c Gyrocopter Fuel crash (spawn_fuel_fraction set to 0.04 in the copy, 49 ticks of throttle, destroy() from Unit._physics_process via _burn_fuel unit.gd:641-650) f=1117->1117; d1 apply_damage after await physics_frame f=1307->1307; d2 apply_damage after await process_frame f=1497 (Engine.is_in_physics_frame false) -> controller tick f=1498 (next step); d3 apply_damage from a priority +5 node f=1687 -> controller tick f=1688. In every same-frame case the notes read: destroy() -> destroyed.emit -> controller _on_unit_destroyed (Token taken, then unit_destroyed.emit) -> ... -> MatchController tick start. Engine.get_physics_frames() reads F for the whole of step F and still F in the idle phase after it (d2). Read: unit.gd:467-480 destroy(), match_controller.gd:196-206, 474-480.
findings.recommendation: The loss check at the end of the controller's tick sees the destruction of the same frame for all four real sources; keep it state-based (has_lost on the ledger each RUNNING tick), so a later source is simply decided one tick later. In the loss scenario assert a Tab+Enter double loss and a lethal-Shot-plus-Tab double loss (timed as in Q4 case 3a) so a change of tree order or priority fails loudly.

findings.question: Q3 (measured). Both Players press Self-destruct on the same tick: do both Unit.destroyed fire in the same physics frame, before the controller's tick of that frame?
findings.answer: Yes. Tab and Enter pressed in one harness step destroy both Units in the same physics frame, P1 first then P2 (their PlayerMatchInputs, tree order), each handled by the controller, and both before that frame's controller tick; the same holds with Input.use_accumulated_input true (the real game default) for keys arriving in the idle phase or at the start of a step.
findings.evidence: MEASURED, pf_q2 a3: Player1Unit destroyed.emit f=582 n=10509, Player2Unit f=582 n=10514, controller tick f=582 n=10516+ (order in the frame: Player1MatchInput destroys P1 -> controller handler (Token taken) -> Player2MatchInput destroys P2 -> controller handler -> ChoiceInputs -> Units -> FireInputs -> MatchController tick). With the prototype loss check (probe copy only) the same press with 1 Token each ends in round_over(-1) (pf_q4 case 3a: P1 Tab + lethal Shot on P2 in frame 98, tokens [0,0], winner -1). pf_acc.log (use_accumulated_input=true): both destroyed at f=10 and f=198, controller tick same frame, for idle-phase and step-start injection. Windowed real-time run (pf_q2_realtime.log, variable steps per frame): same, f=588.
findings.recommendation: none beyond Q2's regression assertions. Note for scenario authors: two presses count as one tick only if they land in the same physics step; one injected a step later is ignored once the first loss paused the tree.

findings.question: Q4 (measured). get_tree().paused = true at the end of MatchController._physics_process: do nodes later in the order still tick in the rest of that frame, and what happens to a destruction that would have happened later in it?
findings.answer: The pause takes effect at once, mid-frame: pausable nodes later in the order (both Weapons, a priority +5 node, a priority-0 node last in tree order) do NOT tick in the rest of that frame; only process_mode ALWAYS nodes do (RoundRestartInput, an ALWAYS +5 probe). A destruction a pausable later node would have made is not made and stays pending until the first unpaused tick (after restart it hit a benched Unit and did nothing). A destruction made by an ALWAYS node after the pause still takes a Token and emits unit_destroyed, but the paused controller never re-checks, so the outcome announced earlier stands. In the real tree nothing that destroys is later than the controller, so nothing is lost: a Shot kill and a Self-destruct in the loss frame are both counted before the decision.
findings.evidence: MEASURED, probe pf_q4 (prototype ledger in the copy, tokens [1,1]; late probe nodes A +5 pausable, B 0 tree-last pausable, C +5 ALWAYS, D -5). Case 1 (loss frame f=15): order ... MatchController tick start, 'OVER winner=1 -> setting paused=true', 'paused is now true; emitting round_over', 'end of controller tick', RoundRestartInput, LateC; NOT ticked in f=15: Player1Weapon, Player2Weapon, LateA, LateB (LateD, before the controller, did). LateA's pending kill ran at the restart frame g=24 as 'apply_damage on Player2Unit alive=false' (no effect). Case 2 (loss f=44): LateC (ALWAYS) apply_damage on P2 after the pause -> destroyed.emit, handler took the Token: tokens [0,0], winner_index 1, round_over calls [(15,1),(44,1)] (one per round, no second). Case 3a (f=98): lethal Shot (priority 0, before controller) + Tab in the same frame -> round_over(-1), tokens [0,0]. Case 3b: the same Shot reparented after the controller: last tick f=151, skipped in loss frame f=152, P2 alive with 1 hp, winner 1, Shot frozen in the 'shots' group and freed by _free_shots at restart g=161. Restart frame (all runs): RoundRestartInput -> restart() (leave_play x2, ledger reset, 'setting paused=false', 'paused=false done') -> round_started -> _free_shots -> then nodes later than RoundRestartInput tick unpaused in that same frame (Weapons, LateA, LateB), but benched Units fire nothing. Identical on Map 01 (pf_q4_map.log). Read: match_controller.gd:196-206; split_screen.tscn:218.
findings.recommendation: Keep the loss decision entirely inside the controller's tick before the pause (as designed). Decide and document what _on_unit_destroyed does while is_round_over(): either return first (no Token, no emit) or accept that a late destruction (ALWAYS node, harness coroutine) takes a Token without changing winner_index. Scenarios that destroy during the pause must expect the second.

findings.question: Q5 (read + measured + pictures). Round ends while a Player is destroyed and choosing (WAITING, no choice): what do that Player's RespawnCountdown, UnitChoice and the Round-over screen show; is anything left over the Round-over panel?
findings.answer: Nothing is left over the panel. On round_over every RespawnCountdown stops counting and hides, every UnitChoice hides, and the Round-over screen shows in both views (last child of each SubViewport, process_mode ALWAYS). Only the HUD band (HP/Fuel/status line, y 16-76) stays visible above the centred panel (x 60-580, y 293.5-426.5). The same holds for the loser destroyed on the loss tick, for a winner who was destroyed earlier and is counting down or has chosen (ready), and for a double loss. Two facts to know: the winner can itself be a destroyed Player (Player 2 wins! while its HUD reads HP 0 / 40), and the unmodified screen prints 'Player 0 wins!' for round_over(-1).
findings.evidence: READ: respawn_countdown.gd:143-145 (shows on unit_destroyed unless is_round_over(), which is still false when the destruction precedes the controller's check), :157-158 (_on_round_over -> _set_counting(false): visible=false, set_process(false)); unit_choice.gd:274-295 (hidden when is_round_over()), :371-372 (_on_round_over hides); round_over_screen.gd:106-109 (winner_index + 1), :124-125; round_over_screen.tscn:17 and split_screen.tscn:164,199 (RoundOver is the last child of each SubViewport: Camera, Countdown, Hud, UnitChoice, RoundOver). unit_destroyed and round_over both fire inside the same physics step, so no rendered frame shows the choice panel and countdown first. MEASURED (pf_q5.log, node dump of every visible Control per view): case A (P1 loser destroyed on the loss tick, P2 alive), case B (P2 destroyed 60 ticks earlier, countdown 'Respawn in 2' and choice panel visible before the loss), case B2 (P2 chose, 'Motorbike ready' panel before the loss), case C (both destroyed on one tick): after round_over RespawnCountdown visible=false processing=false, UnitChoice visible=false, RoundOverScreen visible=true in both views; the only visible Controls are the HUD nodes and the Round-over panel; still true 40 ticks later (paused). Controller while over: is_choosing true for the destroyed Player, seconds_until_respawn frozen (3.00 / 1.97). Case C text 'Player 0 wins!' in both views. Windowed pictures (Metal, Map 01): pf-engine/out/shots/B1_winner_counting_down_before_loss.png, B2_after_loss_winner_was_choosing.png, C_double_loss_both_choosing.png, A_loser_choosing_winner_alive.png.
findings.recommendation: No change needed to hide the countdown and panel. Implement the round_over(-1) text (nobody_text) as designed: the current screen's 'Player 0 wins!' was measured. Consider whether a winner shown as destroyed (HP 0 / 40 in the band) needs a line of design thought; it is a consequence of deciding the winner by Tokens, not a bug.

findings.question: Q6 (read + measured). Unit.destroy() / leave_play(): leave_play emits no destroyed; destroy() on a Unit that is not alive does nothing; Unit.stats is still the type's UnitStats when destroyed fires.
findings.answer: All three confirmed. leave_play() emits hit_points_changed(0) and fuel_changed(0) only, never destroyed; destroy() (and apply_damage()) on a Unit that is not alive return before emitting anything, so a second destroy() is silent; destroy() never touches stats, so when destroyed fires unit.stats is the very UnitStats object of rules.unit_types[i] the Unit was spawned with, and the controller's handler can find the index by type_id or by identity.
findings.evidence: READ: unit.gd:467-480 (destroy: 'if not _is_alive: return', then state, hit_points_changed, fuel_changed, destroyed.emit at 480), :491-503 (leave_play: same guard, emits hit_points_changed and fuel_changed only), :434-441 (apply_damage returns for a not-alive Unit), :669-670 (stats is replaced only in _apply_type via spawn). MEASURED (pf_q6.log): leave_play() on a live Unit: destroyed +0, hit_points_changed +1, fuel_changed +1; leave_play()/destroy()/apply_damage() on the benched Unit: all +0; a spawned Buggy destroyed twice: destroyed +1, handler saw stats.type_id=buggy, unit.type_id=buggy, unit_types.find(unit.stats)=1 (identity) and by type_id 1, is_alive=false, hit_points 0. In pf_q2 the controller's handler read stats.type_id motorbike (x8) and gyrocopter (the Fuel crash). A destruction the garage refuses (Unit spawned behind the controller's back, Player WAITING) emits no unit_destroyed and, with the take placed after note_destroyed accepted, takes no Token (warning at garage_queue.gd:285).
findings.recommendation: Take the Token only after _garage.note_destroyed() returned true, reading unit.stats.type_id in the handler, as designed. Prefer find-by-identity (unit_types.find(unit.stats)) with a type_id fallback, or reject duplicate type_ids in TokenLedger.first_problem(): UnitStats.first_problem() (unit_stats.gd:263-270) checks neither uniqueness nor emptiness of type_id.

findings.question: Q7 (read + measured). After restart() from a Round that ended by a loss, can a Shot in flight (frozen by the pause) or a stale choice make a Token or a Unit be counted twice? Order of _free_shots against round_started.
findings.answer: No. restart() unpauses and then emits round_started synchronously, and SplitScreen._free_shots is a round_started listener, so frozen Shots are set non-processing and freed before any physics tick can run them (and they sit before RoundRestartInput in the order, so they cannot tick in the restart frame anyway). The standing choice is cleared by bench(), restart() takes no Token and emits no destroyed, and a Token is taken once per destroyed.emit.
findings.evidence: READ: match_controller.gd:255-265 (restart: seat flags, bench x2, state RUNNING, paused=false at 264, round_started.emit at 265); split_screen.gd:139-141 (begin first, then round_started.connect(_free_shots) and _restock_fuel_cans), :185-188 (set_physics_process(false) + queue_free for the 'shots' group); garage_queue.gd:218-228 (bench clears _choice at 227). MEASURED (pf_q7.log, also pf_q7_map.log on Map 01): 7a Shot fired f=32, loss f=34, Shot frozen at (-1.4,0.5,0.0) for 60 paused ticks, restart g=98: RoundRestartInput -> leave_play x2 -> 'setting paused=false' -> 'paused=false done' -> '_free_shots: 1 shots in group' -> 'round_started emitted'; no Shot tick afterwards, Shot freed, no hit_points_changed beyond the bench, unit_destroyed +1 (the Tab), tokens [1,1]. CONTROL with _free_shots disconnected: the same Shot resumes at f=242 (frame after restart g=241) and ticks f=242-246. 7b P2 had chosen (chosen_type_index 0, seconds_until_respawn 2.47) when P1 lost; after restart chosen -1, is_choosing true, seconds_until_respawn 0.00, and no unit_spawned in 250 ticks without a key. 7c loss -> restart -> loss: unit_destroyed +1, restart +0, tokens [1,1] after restart, then +1 again. 7e Enter and a lethal Shot on P2 in one frame: one destroyed.emit, one Token (99->98). 7d Tab and R pressed on one step restart the Round inside the loss tick (see risks).
findings.recommendation: Keep ledger.start() before round_started.emit() in restart() (the order bench -> state -> ledger -> paused=false -> round_started is what the UI listeners need). Keep _free_shots connected to round_started; never move it after a physics tick.

findings.question: Else A (measured). TokenStock fixtures made in code: what does the engine do with the typed Dictionary[StringName, int]?
findings.answer: A dictionary literal assigned to the typed property works; an untyped Dictionary variable assigned to counts raises a runtime SCRIPT ERROR (the function aborts); counts[&"id"] = n and counts["id"] = n both work (String keys are stored as StringName; floats convert to int; negatives are accepted); count_of() reads String and StringName ids alike. Resource.duplicate() SHARES the counts Dictionary with the original (writing into the copy changed the cached shipped stock); duplicate(true) and duplicate_deep() give an independent typed copy; TokenStock.new() instances do not share.
findings.evidence: MEASURED, probe_kit/typed_dict.gd and typed_dict2.gd (godot -s): 'Invalid assignment of property or key counts with value of type Dictionary on a base object of type Resource (TokenStock)'; duplicate(): shipped truck=77 after the copy was set to 77; duplicate(true) and duplicate_deep(): shipped stays 2, typed_key 21 (StringName) typed_value 2 (int); shipped stock read through unit_types ids = motorbike 5, buggy 3, truck 2, gyrocopter 2. src/gameplay/maps/token_stock.gd:20-21 says 'duplicate() it for a private copy', which is wrong for counts.
findings.recommendation: In token_kit.gd and the runner build fixtures with TokenStock.new() plus a dictionary literal (or counts[key] = n); use duplicate_deep() when copying the shipped stock; never assign an untyped Dictionary variable. Correct the token_stock.gd class doc line that recommends duplicate().

findings.question: Else B (measured). Timing facts a scenario author needs.
findings.answer: A key event injected by the harness at the start of physics step F, or in the idle phase after step F, is first seen by the input nodes in step F+1 (a_just_pressed stamp); level-triggered reads are not delayed. The Round-restart key (R) and the choice and Self-destruct keys are edge-read, so a scenario must wait at least two ticks after pressing before reading a loss or a restart.
findings.evidence: MEASURED: pf_q2 a1 stimulus read at frame 14 -> destroyed f=15; a1b idle-phase injection read 393 -> f=394; with use_accumulated_input true (pf_acc) the same. Harness doc split_screen_harness.gd:34-36 and the 'acts one tick later' note agree.
findings.recommendation: Use Kit.press_settled (press + 1 tick) and then at least one more tick before asserting; do not compare the press frame with the destruction frame for equality.

findings.question: Else C (measured). Cursor skip in PlayerChoiceInput: in which tick can it first act?
findings.answer: PlayerChoiceInput (priority -1) runs before Units and Shots (0) but after the same Player's PlayerMatchInput, so after a Self-destruct the Player is already 'choosing' in that very frame's ChoiceInput tick, while after a Shot kill or a Fuel crash the first ChoiceInput tick with is_choosing true is the NEXT frame. UnitChoice has been refreshed on unit_destroyed in between, so for one rendered frame the cursor may rest on a 0-Token slot.
findings.evidence: MEASURED order, pf_q2 frame orders (Self-destruct frame: PlayerMatchInput destroys, then Player1ChoiceInput; Shot-kill frame: Player2ChoiceInput ran before the Shot tick). Read: player_choice_input.gd:87-100, unit_choice.gd:274-295.
findings.recommendation: Do the skip to a type with Tokens in the same place that decides the cursor mark: either on the controller's unit_destroyed/round_started signal (immediate, state-based) or first thing in the tick that finds is_choosing true, before the confirm check; the design's rule that a 0-Token slot never wears the mark already hides the one-frame gap.

corrections: Replace the design's 'Unit and Shot ticks run BEFORE the controller' by the measured order Drive/Match/Choice inputs (-1), then Map nodes, Units, FireInputs, Shots, MatchController, RoundRestartInput (0, tree order), then Weapons (+1); the Weapon is the last node of the frame, not before the Shot.
State in the loss scenarios that an injected key acts one physics step after the injection, and wait at least two ticks after Kit.press before reading a loss or a restart.

Build TokenStock fixtures with TokenStock.new() and a dictionary literal or counts[key] = n, never with an untyped Dictionary variable (runtime error) or Resource.duplicate() (shares counts with the cached .tres; use duplicate_deep()), and fix the token_stock.gd class doc line that recommends duplicate().

Take the Token only after _garage.note_destroyed() accepted and read unit.stats.type_id (or find unit.stats in unit_types by identity) in the handler; add a duplicate/empty type_id check to TokenLedger.first_problem() or use identity so a duplicate id cannot decrement the wrong type.

Decide in the class doc what _on_unit_destroyed does while the Round is OVER (a destruction by an ALWAYS node or a harness coroutine during the pause takes a Token and emits unit_destroyed but cannot change winner_index), instead of leaving it implicit.
risks: The 'same tick' guarantee rests on default priority 0 plus tree position (World before MatchController), not on a declared priority: moving MatchController before World, or giving a Unit, Shot or Map node a later priority, shifts Shot/Fuel-crash destructions to the next frame (measured: a priority +5 source is decided one frame later and a double loss could be split). Mitigate with the Tab+Enter and lethal-Shot-plus-Tab regression assertions; if the order is ever made explicit, store the priority in the scene because World's inputs read the controller's priority in their own _ready() before the controller's _ready() runs.

A destruction after the decision (an ALWAYS-mode node or a harness coroutine, both keep running while paused) takes a Token and emits unit_destroyed while the Round is OVER: measured tokens [0,0] with winner_index 1, so a winner can show 0 Tokens; benign because restart() resets the ledger, but the HUD token label under the Round-over panel would show it.

R pressed on the very tick of the loss restarts the Round inside that tick (RoundRestartInput runs right after the controller and is ALWAYS): measured Tab+R on one step, round_over then restart in frame 680, the loss is never shown. Either accept it or ignore the restart key for a few ticks after round_over.

A destruction source in the idle phase (a future _process hazard or UI button) would be decided one physics step later and the choice panel and 'Respawn in 3' would be drawn for one rendered frame before the Round-over screen replaces them (measured d2: controller tick the next step); today the game has none.

The winner can be a destroyed Player: the screen says 'Player 2 wins!' while that Player's HUD reads HP 0 / 40 and Fuel 0 / 100 (picture B2). A consequence of deciding by Tokens, but it may read oddly in the evidence frames.
The unmodified RoundOverScreen prints 'Player 0 wins!' for round_over(-1) (picture C), so the nobody_text branch is required, not optional.

SplitScreen._free_shots frees frozen Shots only because it is connected to round_started (control run: without it the Shot resumes the tick after the restart and flies on); the connection is made after begin() (split_screen.gd:139-141) so the first round_started does not call it, which is fine, but it must stay a round_started listener.

I worked on the pre-rename snapshot (HEAD 8e09d55 content under snap-head); all file:line references are to those files. The orchestrator's rename changes identifiers (canister to flag) and doc lines, not the order or pause facts measured here, but line numbers in the renamed repo files will differ.

NOT DETERMINED: behaviour of the loop with several physics steps inside one rendered frame under a real stall (my windowed real-time run on a ProMotion Mac showed the same relations, but I did not force 2-3 steps per frame); in-step order is engine-defined and does not depend on it. The ledger and loss check I ran are a throwaway prototype in the probe copy of match_controller.gd, not the implementation: the facts about order, pause, UI and restart are independent of its details.
